slices.focus: A neighbor invites Ayaka to a weekend watercolor class where clumsily sketching ferries and cranes becomes a surprisingly calming non-work practice.
slices.summary: Neighbor Kuroda Miki invites Ayaka to a small weekend watercolor class. Despite being clumsy at it, Ayaka finds the class strangely calming — she sketches familiar harbor infrastructure (ferries, cranes, waiting benches) from memory, transforming them from problems-to-solve into shapes and colors. The class and a light hallway friendship with Miki become ordinary life support: low-pressure, inexpensive, and locally rooted.
open_loops: Hobby could become another project if over-structured
Budget constraint means supplies must stay cheap
